stops.title: Spider-Man
stops.fight: The Green Goblin makes Spider-Man choose between saving Mary Jane or a cable car full of kids on the Queensboro Bridge. After that, they have their final fight in an old abandoned building on Roosevelt Island.
stops.why: It made about $822 million worldwide, which showed that superhero movies could be huge hits years before the Marvel Cinematic Universe even started.
stops.fact: The cable car in this scene is based on the real Roosevelt Island Tramway, which people still ride over the East River today.

stops.title: Spider-Man 2
stops.place: Doctor Octopus's lair on the Hudson River
stops.fight: Spider-Man finds Doctor Octopus at his lair on the waterfront, where Doc Ock's fusion reactor is out of control and about to destroy the city.
stops.why: It won the Oscar for Best Visual Effects, and a lot of people still rank it as one of the best superhero movies ever made.
stops.fact: The famous train fight in this movie was actually filmed on Chicago's elevated trains, not in New York. Doc Ock's lair was a model and a set that were based on the old Pier 56.

stops.title: Spider-Man 3
stops.fight: Venom and Sandman team up and hang Mary Jane in a web high above a construction site.
stops.why: It made the most money out of the three Raimi movies, almost $900 million worldwide, but critics didn't like how many villains were crammed into it.
stops.fact: The construction site was made with computer graphics, so it isn't a real place you can go to. Some of the street scenes were filmed in Cleveland, Ohio.

stops.title: The Amazing Spider-Man
stops.place: The roof of Oscorp Tower, Midtown
stops.fight: Spider-Man climbs Oscorp Tower to stop the Lizard from releasing a chemical cloud that would turn everyone in the city into lizards.
stops.why: It retold Spider-Man's origin story only ten years after the first movie, this time with Andrew Garfield and Emma Stone.
stops.fact: Oscorp Tower doesn't exist. It's a fake skyscraper that was added to the Manhattan skyline with visual effects.

stops.title: The Amazing Spider-Man 2
stops.fight: Electro's first big fight with Spider-Man knocks out all of the screens in Times Square.
stops.why: It made about $709 million worldwide, which is the least of any live-action Spider-Man movie, and Sony canceled its plans for more sequels after it.
stops.fact: Times Square is the fight most people remember, but the final battles in the movie happen at a power plant and a clock tower, and both of those were made up for the movie.

stops.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
stops.fight: Spider-Man fights the Vulture on a stolen Avengers cargo plane, and it ends up crash landing on the beach at Coney Island.
stops.why: It was the first solo Spider-Man movie in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which happened after Sony agreed to share the character with Marvel Studios.
stops.fact: Most of Homecoming was actually filmed in and around Atlanta, Georgia, not New York.

stops.title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
stops.fight: Miles and the Spider-People from other universes fight Kingpin inside his Super-Collider while it rips open portals to other dimensions.
stops.why: It won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature, and it made Miles Morales, an Afro-Latino Spider-Man, the main character of a movie.
stops.fact: The animators mixed computer animation with hand-drawn comic book dots and lines, and a lot of animated movies have copied that style since then.

stops.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
stops.fight: Mysterio sends an army of drones to attack London, and Spider-Man has to fight his way through them and all of Mysterio's illusions around Tower Bridge.
stops.why: It was the first Spider-Man movie to make more than $1 billion worldwide.
stops.fact: It's the only live-action Spider-Man movie where the final fight happens outside of New York.

stops.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
stops.actor: Tom Holland, Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield
stops.fight: Villains from other universes fight all three Spider-Men on the Statue of Liberty.
stops.why: It brought back Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield, so all three live-action Spider-Men were in one movie together. It made about $1.9 billion worldwide.
stops.fact: The statue is covered in scaffolding in the movie because it's being fitted with a giant Captain America shield.

stops.title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
stops.fight: Miles runs from universe to universe, from Mumbattan to the Spider-Society's headquarters, and ends up in a different version of his own Brooklyn.
stops.why: It made about $690 million worldwide, which is way more than the first one, and it was nominated for the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.
stops.fact: It ends on a cliffhanger, and the story is supposed to finish in Beyond the Spider-Verse.

stops.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
stops.fight: Spider-Man fights the Hand, a group of ninjas being controlled by Jean Grey, at Damage Control's facility on Roosevelt Island.
stops.why: It passed $2 billion worldwide in August 2026, which makes it the highest-grossing Spider-Man movie so far.
stops.fact: The New York fight was reportedly filmed at an old prison in Dorset, England. It's also kind of cool that the map ends on the same island where it started in 2002.
